title: Matrix row scan
statement: Let $x$ be a finite bit string, $B$ a natural number, $P$ a proposition, and $σ=(p,n,a,b,s,t,tmp,st,nx)$ a program register state. Suppose $2|x|+2\le B$, every register of $σ$ is at most $B$, $a\le s<n$, $p=2n+2+2an$, $b\le n$, and $2n+2+2n^2\le |x|$. Assume that for every $b'\le n$, the program started at the column-check stage with row register $s$, column register $b'$, and pointer $2n+2+2sn$ terminates with all registers bounded by $B$ and has an accepting computation exactly when $P$ holds. Then the program started at the row-scan stage in state $σ$ terminates with all registers bounded by $B$ and has an accepting computation exactly when $P$ holds.
hypotheses_covered: all nine registers of $\u001bσ$ are at most $B$
for every $b'\le n$, the stated column-check configuration has the specified termination, register bound, and acceptance semantics
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, $P$ a proposition, and $σ$ a register
configuration whose nine register values are all at most $B$. Suppose $2|x|+2\le B$, the
row register $a$ is at most the source register $s$, $s<n$, the input pointer is
$2n+2+2an$, the column register $b$ is at most $n$, and $2n+2+2n^2\le |x|$. If, for
every column $b'\le n$, starting the fixed path program at its column-check stage with
row register $s$, column register $b'$, and input pointer $2n+2+2sn$ terminates within
the register bound and accepts exactly when $P$ holds, then starting at its row-scan
stage with configuration $σ$ terminates within the register bound and accepts exactly
when $P$ holds.
